facts.raw_span: A man in his 40s
weighing 109kg
stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias on his lower right lateral shin
the lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels were observed, with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
the epidermis was normal
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R identified as the only somatic mutation

concepts.why: The patient's vascular lesion, characterized by telangiectasias and superficial small-caliber vessels, combined with the KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation, suggests a diagnosis of Angiosarcoma, a malignant vascular tumor.

The patient's history of radiation therapy and the development of a vascular lesion with telangiectasias and a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation suggest a diagnosis of Radiation-Induced Angiosarcoma.
The patient's history of stage IV rectal adenocarcinoma and the development of a skin lesion with vascular features suggest a diagnosis of Cutaneous Metastasis of Rectal Adenocarcinoma.
The patient's skin lesion is characterized by telangiectasias, which are dilated blood vessels, suggesting a diagnosis of Telangiectasia.
The patient's skin lesion is characterized by superficial small-caliber vessels and telangiectasias, suggesting a diagnosis of Vascular Malformation.
The patient's vascular lesion, combined with the KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation, suggests a diagnosis of Kaposi's Sarcoma, a malignant vascular tumor.
The patient's skin lesion is characterized by a bright red plaque with telangiectasias, suggesting a diagnosis of Cherry Angioma.
The patient's skin lesion is characterized by superficial small-caliber vessels and telangiectasias, suggesting a diagnosis of Pyogenic Granuloma.

rationales.F03: The patient's history of rectal adenocarcinoma increases the likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F04: The presence of pulmonary and liver metastases suggests a high tumor burden, increasing the likelihood of cutaneous metastasis.
rationales.F05: Radiation therapy is a known risk factor for the development of angiosarcoma.
rationales.F06: The presence of a well-defined, blanchable red plaque with telangiectasias is suggestive of a vascular lesion.
rationales.F08: The histopathological findings of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels are consistent with a diagnosis of angiosarcoma or other vascular lesions.
rationales.F10: The identification of a somatic mutation in the KDR (VEGFR2) gene is consistent with a diagnosis of angiosarcoma.
